## About the Blog

**Status Quo** is an independent publication and interconnected writing archive by **Neeraj Paulose Raj (NPR)**.

Most blogs present articles as a disposable reverse-chronological stream: an essay is published, read for a few days, and then buried beneath newer posts. But real-world questions—whether about biometric state surveillance, digital privacy, constitutional jurisprudence, market failures, or community governance—do not exist in isolation. They connect, contradict, and build on one another over years.

This site structures essays and underlying concepts as a **networked knowledge graph**:
- **Law:** Legal regimes, constitutional questions, rights, digital privacy jurisprudence, courts, and statutory frameworks.
- **Society:** The broader social order—encompassing public policy, economic mechanisms, incentives, political dynamics, community governance, and culture.

## How to Navigate: List & Graph Views

1. **List View:** Read complete long-form essays and analytical entries. Within every piece, you’ll find Wikipedia-style `[[wikilinks]]` pointing to underlying concepts, as well as an automatically updated **Connected Concepts** and **Referenced In (Backlinks)** section showing which other essays or ideas connect to it.
2. **Graph View:** An interactive, force-directed topological map. Explore how legal principles intersect with societal and economic forces. Click any node to center its local neighborhood (1–2 hops), view its summary, or open the piece.

## Read & Subscribe

All essays are published concurrently on Substack at [**statusquotoday.substack.com**](https://statusquotoday.substack.com). You can subscribe there for free to receive new dispatches directly in your inbox.
